steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Media language refers to the ways in which media products communicate meaning to audiences through visual, audio, written, and technical codes.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Denotation is the literal or surface meaning of a sign (what you see). Connotation is the deeper or associated meaning (what it suggests). For example, a red rose denotes a flower but connotes love and romance.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Technical codes include camerawork (close-up, wide shot, low angle), editing (cross-cutting, montage, pace), sound (diegetic, non-diegetic, sound bridge), and mise-en-scene (setting, costume, lighting, props).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Symbolic codes convey meaning through objects, colours, and visual elements that carry cultural significance — e.g. a wedding ring symbolises commitment, dark lighting connotes danger.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use specific examples from CSPs when discussing media language Identify the code FIRST, then explain what it connotes — don't just describe what you see Use the correct terminology: 'connote' not 'mean', 'signifier' not 'sign'
